title: A Cipher for the Asset
premise: Odile Crane, a whistle-blower living under four names, discovers her safe house listed for sale online — the photos revealing her hiding place, her documents, her face reflected in a window. The listing is bait, and the fisher is the agency she betrayed, using her to lure Marek Voss, a defector carrying proof of their crimes. Odile realizes she is both target and asset: if she runs, they take Voss; if she stays, they take her. Infiltrating the extraction network that once protected her, she must decide whether Voss is a witness or a weapon aimed at her. At the border checkpoint, as shifts change in the fog before dawn, Odile trades herself for his passage — then burns the archive's last copy of her own file, choosing love and justice outside the law over survival by erasure.
about_author: Silas Whitlock spent eleven years as a logistics analyst for humanitarian convoys across Eastern Europe, where he learned that borders are less lines than moods. He writes thrillers from a farmhouse whose location he declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The House That Sold Itself
chapters.summary: Odile Crane — currently 'Nadia' — spots her safe house on a real estate site, every room photographed, including the closet where her go-bag sits. Her handler goes silent when she calls. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the cold vertigo of realizing your paranoia was calibrated exactly right, one hour too late.

chapters.title: Bait and the Baited
chapters.summary: Odile traces the listing to a shell firm and finds Marek Voss, the defector she was meant to never meet, already hiding nearby — the agency wants them found together. A former extraction contact, Tomas, offers help but demands she verify Voss's archive first. POV: Odile, with an interlude from Voss. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into reluctant trust.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: The archive checks out but reveals Odile's own name among the betrayed — the agency sold her years ago. With the checkpoint rotation shifting at dawn, Tomas's plan requires a decoy at the crossing. Odile volunteers, knowing what it costs. POV: alternating Odile and Voss. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; love declared in logistics, not words.

chapters.title: What the Fog Keeps
chapters.summary: At the checkpoint, Odile walks the decoy route while Voss crosses in a maintenance convoy; she is taken, interrogated, and offered her old life back if she recants. Instead she recites the archive aloud until her captors realize the story is already out. Released into fog with nothing but a new fifth name, she finds Voss waiting anyway. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — justice done, duty abandoned, love chosen.
